findings.target: engine A TQ3 (twist entries with beta letters)
findings.claim: Engine A reports betabeta = 0, beta b -> beta dc = 0, beta b -> gamma gamma = 0 (and betagamma = 0) on the twisted letters and concludes that b-gamma is the only nonzero twist entry; these zeros are artifacts of silent rounding. Corrected: betabeta, beta b -> beta dc and beta b -> gamma gamma are nonzero; betagamma = 0 is genuine.
findings.evidence: step2/twoletter/engine_a/src.nosync/ea_kern.py contract() converts products of letter components with int(round(.)) without a check; A builds the beta letters as dual rows of the weight basis, entries +-1/16, +-i/16, so every term vanishes (qa/out.nosync/bisect_A.json: zero whenever the letters are the twisted betas, even with generic xi and outputs). With the letters multiplied by 16, A gives betabeta = (2/3) c_gamma + (1/3 - 2 log(3/2)) c_dc per unit letters on gamma^K, K the complement of I and J, holomorphic derivatives only, both colour words equal; beta b -> beta dc = -(64/3) c_beta (one colour word); beta b -> gamma gamma = (8/3)(c1h1 c2h0 - c1h0 c2h1) (qa/out.nosync/twistA_fixed.json). A with integer letters equals B's code exactly at four momenta, and B's code on A's twisted data has the same eps_IJK structure (twist_B_on_A2.json). b-gamma is unaffected (gamma and b letters are Gaussian integers; linear in its 1/2-entry outputs).
findings.fix: Make contract() exact (Fraction arithmetic or an assertion as in qa_core.gq); rerun TQ3 and every A computation whose letter vectors are not Gaussian integers; replace the TQ3 summary. Audit the two-letter and Part-C engine A callers of contract() for non-integer letters.

findings.target: engine A TQ4 c_Q, results.json two_component
findings.claim: A states {S^(1)(xi),O} = -F1 and c_Q = 2 log(3/2) - theta_perp - p_perp; the classical component is +F1, so the two-body part of c_Q is -2 log(3/2) (as engine B) and c_Q = -2 log(3/2) - theta_perp - p_perp.
findings.evidence: The quadratic functional -(Gamma(xi,lam),A^*) induces lam -> +Gamma(xi,lam) under the reading fixed by Prop c1-Q (int(dc,A^*) <-> Qc = -dc); Cor c7-Q states that the classical component replaces A by Gamma(Q_1,lam) and gives the first functional F1. Both engines find the engine arrows opposite to Lemma qs-arrows (A: ratio -2 incl. vertex scale; B: finding F1), yet A takes the classical sign from that Lemma. Both engines agree on the computed coefficient of F1, -2 log(3/2).
findings.fix: Set {S^(1)(xi),O} = +F1 in A's TQ4 and two-component tables; report c_Q = -2 log(3/2) - theta_perp - p_perp (units u).

findings.claim: Lemma qs-arrows has the wrong overall sign: xi. maps lam -> +Gamma(xi,lam) and A -> +(1/2) rho(dA) xi. The C_xi plane-wave component is +i(p,Gamma(xi,lam)|_V), Example qs-cubic should read {S^(1)(xi),A_perp} contains +Gamma(xi,lam)|_perp, and the composite line is real (-+2 xi e^{-2 eps|p|^2}/|p|^2), not +-2i as in Rem qs-twocomp.
findings.evidence: Prop c1-Q reading (free action eq c1-free); engine B gate E0-conv/E0-xi-arrows; engine A E0 ratio -2; Cor c7-Q; both engines compute the composite line real with c x lam negative.
findings.fix: Flip the sign in Lemma qs-arrows, Prop qs-comm (i) plane-wave formula, Example qs-cubic and Rem qs-twocomp.

findings.claim: Route B never places the cubic term T5 with its lam* leg as the output (S3 blocks are generated only at outputs of type A), a placement required by Def qs-defect (i) and listed in Rem qs-placements and in B's own census (T5b). B's published n = 0 tables survive (the omitted configurations cancel there), but every n >= 1 leg set with a lam* output is wrong in route B, so B cannot serve as the second route for the n >= 1 tables and the derivative-letter twist entries.
findings.evidence: qb_job.py: "if SLOT[self.outs[j]][0] != 'A': continue". A-vs-B n=1: (A_V, A_perp) -> (c, lam*) with d_0 on A_V, A = (226-206i)(1+2 log(3/2)) [seeded data], B = 0. Emulating the omission inside engine A (T5 restricted to A outputs, qa/out.nosync/T5b_emulate.json) reproduces B's 0 exactly; the placement split (T5b_split*.json) puts the whole value in the T5 configurations with lam* output, whose line and special-edge parts cancel exactly at n = 0 on (A_V,A_V), (A_V,A_perp), (A_perp,A_perp) -> (c, lam*); on the three-output lam* leg sets at n = 0 the T5 value comes from A outputs only.
findings.fix: Add the S3 placement with a lam*_+- output (cycle legs A, A) to DJob.sequences before any n >= 1 run of route B.

findings.claim: A's G-R1 pass is obtained with an inconsistent bookkeeping: C = {S^(1)(xi), L_1^(0)(O)} is formed as the difference of the two orderings of the even-odd output pair (c, A_V), which forces C = 0, while L_1^(0)(O) itself is formed as their sum and is nonzero; it also uses {S,O} = -F1 and A_V <- -Gamma. With one consistent convention the relation still holds.
findings.evidence: qa/out.nosync/r1_check.json, r1_check2.json: with k the common data factor and L = log(3/2): s(a3 F3) = -2Lk, L_1^(0)(F1) = b1 - b2 = -k (two odd outputs), {S^(1)(xi), L_1^(0)(O)} = v1 + v2 = (1+2L)k (A_V -> +Gamma); the sum vanishes exactly, separately in the rational and log(3/2) parts. This confirms a3 = 4 log(3/2) relative to the arity-zero kernels.
findings.fix: Rewrite qa_r1.py with the Grassmann reordering sign of the outputs, {S,O} = +F1 and A_V <- +Gamma(xi,lam)|_V; report the three terms.

findings.target: engine A TQ3 b-gamma reduction; theory Thm qs-twistcheck
findings.claim: A reduces b-gamma "modulo total derivatives" and concludes that both colour orders give (128/3) c_gamma with all log(3/2) terms in total derivatives. Total derivatives of local operators are not trivial in the cohomology of Q^xi_0 (O = int omega f with arbitrary omega), so this is not a valid comparison with [BK, (3.68)]. Modulo Im Q^xi_0 only (the derivative on dc is the u'-component of the Dirac equation), the two colour words are 64/3 - 128 log(3/2) and 32 + 64 log(3/2) (A normalisation), unequal and with log(3/2).
findings.evidence: engine A results.json TQ3 rows bgamma; q1_targets T6 (BK (3.68) has equal coefficients for the two words).
findings.fix: Reduce only modulo Im Q^xi_0 (exact derivatives u sigma d and the Dirac-equation component), and compare with [BK] only at the class level (relations (3.59)-(3.63) through the tree-level psl(3|3) commutant, with the R_1/S_1 terms), as Thm qs-twistcheck (d) requires.

findings.target: both engines: completeness of Part Q
findings.claim: The action side TQ1 (Ob^(1)(xi), particular solution p_V, p_perp, theta_V - theta_perp) is computed by neither engine, so c_Q, the trace coefficients and all one-body kernels of Q_1, S_1, K_1 are undetermined; Upsilon_xixi (bc with b = F, bb) is missing; A omits the finite special vertices on rows with D >= 2 (its n >= 1 tables are then eps^0 parts, not kernels); relations R2-R6, the Konishi relation through D_1, G-R4 twisted closure and the class-level twist comparison were not run.
findings.evidence: engine notes and results.json open lists of both engines; engine_spec.json tasks TQ1, TQ3 (arity two), TQ8, gates G-Ob, G-R2..R6, G-twist (d).
findings.fix: Run TQ1 first (Prop qs-freexi (ii) needs the cubic part), then the finite special vertices in A, Upsilon_xixi, and the relations on the bilinears after the psi-shift of Q8.

findings.target: theory Prop qs-rel, Rem qs-bilinears; TQ4 trace coefficients
findings.claim: The relations of Prop qs-rel assume L_1^(0) = 0 on the family, but at psi = 0 L_1^(0)(O) = -(2+4 log(3/2)) u (w1,w2) int omega (dc, A_V) on the trace bilinear (Rem c5-cocycle type). The finite part that removes it, O -> O + y (w1,w2) int omega (A_V,A_V), adds Upsilon_xi(A_V,A_V) to Q_1 of the trace bilinear and changes the reported a2, a3, a4; the values 4 log(3/2) are those of a non-cocycle representative. Rem qs-bilinears calls the relations a finite computation with the (A_perp,A_perp), (A_perp,lam) kernels only.
findings.evidence: engine A notes (L_1^(0)(O) value), verified nonzero here (r1_check.json: v1 = v2 != 0); Rem c5-cocycle; Def c10-hyp (ii).
findings.fix: State the psi-shift in Rem qs-bilinears, include the (A_V,A_V) kernels in the trace part, and report a2..a4 in the psi with L_1^(0) = 0.

findings.claim: C_xi has only the components A*|_V -> lam and lam* -> A|_V besides lam -> c and c* -> lam*; the A*|_perp and A|_perp parts cancel.
findings.evidence: xi.Q^GF a = -rho(d)rho(a) xi and Q^GF xi. a = +rho(d)rho(a) xi for a = A*|_perp (independent check), leaving (d.a) xi on A*|_V; engine B finding F2. The variation kernel V_xi then has components lam (x) A_V, A_V (x) lam, c (x) lam*, lam* (x) c.
findings.fix: Restrict the components to V in Prop qs-comm (i) and Cor qs-edges (i).

findings.claim: eta. is not x^mu xi_mu. + eta^0.: the operator induced by int x^mu S_2(xi_mu) contains the constant antifield arrows Y produced by integrating x^mu by parts; [eta.,Q] = 0 holds only with them.
findings.evidence: engine B gates E0-eta-ep/em (comm_Q without Y fails). The kernels are unaffected (both engines use the functional S^(1)(eta)).
findings.fix: Add Y to the decomposition of eta. and to the formulas for [eta.,Q], [eta.,Q^GF].

findings.claim: For gauge-variant letters the pole identity read pair by pair needs the vacuum-pole x spectator terms (ct_1(AA) from the cubic part of {S^(1)(xi),O}, ct1_xi(c,lam_+)|_0 from sO); the gate description "pair by pair" omits them.

findings.target: engines A and B: orientation of V
findings.claim: Under the identity on vector indices the engines use opposite orientations: A's lam_+ (and A's S_+ (x) W) is B's lam_- (S_- (x) W^*). The scalar results coincide by the mirror symmetry (verified exactly in B's code), but the two-component (undotted/dotted) labels of one engine are reversed relative to step2/notation/dictionary.json.
findings.evidence: revise.nosync/ferm_map/spinor_map.json (A_lamP -> B components 8..15); qa/out.nosync/mirror_B.json; B gate E0-orient ties its labels to the dictionary orientation.
findings.fix: Fix A's two-component labels against the dictionary orientation (or state A's engine-index map to m explicitly).

findings.claim: Neither engine tested T-independence on a K_b defect cycle: B's endpoint test is on the T5 cycle along xi, A has it by construction. Independently, the mechanism and the manuscript coefficients check: the n = 1 cycle has T-dependence eps/(T(T+eps)) and O(eps/T), and the K_b composite line has T d/dT -> -3b/(16 pi^2) (scalar), 3/(8 pi^2) with fibre factors.
findings.fix: Run route B at T|p|^2 in {1,4,16} on one K_b intrinsic cycle with the A_V--c line on the cycle.

findings.target: engine B finding F8 / gate G-closed
findings.claim: The closed form 16 pi^2 [eps^-1] = F/(n_t^2 (n_t-1)(n_t-1)!) is quoted for "every leg set with D = 0", which has no pole; it is the simplex weight for a constant F_1 (degree-2 numerator). The eps^0 formula F log(n_t/(n_t-1))/(n_t-1)! is right (n_t = 2: log 2, checked).
findings.fix: Restate F8 with F_m constant for the pole formula.
